questions.qtext:
Consider a function findCLL that takes a doubly circular linked list head and an integer value as input.

One example of doubly circular linked list is given below –

def findCLL(first, n):
 while first.value != n:
 first = first.next
 if first.value == n:
 return 1
 else:
 return -1


Consider two statements $\text{S1}$ and $\text{S2}$ given below.

  • $\text{S1}:$ Function returns $1$ if there exists a value in linked list
  • $\text{S2}:$ Function returns $-1$ if value does not exist in linked list

Which of the following is the correct option.
questions.solution:
Answer: A

Source solution 1 (score: 5)

Here let us take the given circular doubly linked list as the example

Say we need to find element 4

in the while loop we move forward 4 nodes as first → value != 4

when we arrive at 5th node first → value == 4 so we break out from the loop

if condition is also satisfied as first → value == 4

so we return 1

so S1 is TRUE

Now say we need to find element say 6

here when we check the value of each node with 6 in the while loop there is not hit because 6 is not present in the circular doubly linked list and more over the loop will break only when the we can find the element that we need

So if the element that we need to find is not present in linked list we go into “ INFINITE LOOP “

which means we cant return anything so S2 is FALSE

Finally option A is correct

Source solution 2 (score: 2)

Explanation:
S1: The function correctly traverses the circular linked list and returns 1 if the value n is found. Hence, S1 is True.
S2: The function does not handle the circular nature of the list correctly. If n does not exist in the list, the loop can become infinite since there is no explicit break condition to stop traversal after one full cycle. Thus, S2 is False.

questions.qtext:
Given a doubly linked list where each node has two references (prev and next): one that points to a previous node and another that points to a next node. Assume the linked list below and provide the output for the following two lines.

The list is restored to its initial state before each line executes:

Line1: print(head.next.next.next.prev.prev.data)
Line2: print(tail.prev.prev.prev.prev.next.next.data)

Which of the options is correct.

options.text: Output of line $1$ is $7$ and Output of line $2$ is $9$
Output of line $1$ is $9$ and Output of line $2$ is $7$

questions.solution:
Answer: A

Source solution 1 (score: 2)

Line1: head.next.next.next.prev.prev.data

head.next is a reference to the node containing the value 7.

Similarly, head.next.next.next is a reference to the node containing 5.

node(5).prev.prev is a reference to the node containing 7.

node(7).data = 7

Line2: tail.prev.prev.prev.prev.next.next.data

tail is the reference to the node containing 1.

node(1).prev.prev.prev.prev is the reference to the node containing 3.

node(3).next.next is the reference to the node containing 9.

node(9).data = 9.

Source solution 2 (score: 1)

The correct answer is A. Output of line 1 is 7 and Output of line 2 is 9.

Explanation:

  1. Line 1: print(head.next.next.next.prev.prev.data)

    • head points to 3.
    • head.next points to 7.
    • head.next.next points to 9.
    • head.next.next.next points to 5.
    • head.next.next.next.prev points to 9.
    • head.next.next.next.prev.prev points to 7.
    • head.next.next.next.prev.prev.data is 7.

  2. Line 2: print(tail.prev.prev.prev.prev.next.next.data)

    • tail points to 1.
    • tail.prev points to 5.
    • tail.prev.prev points to 9.
    • tail.prev.prev.prev points to 7.
    • tail.prev.prev.prev.prev points to 3.
    • tail.prev.prev.prev.prev.next points to 7.
    • tail.prev.prev.prev.prev.next.next points to 9.
    • tail.prev.prev.prev.prev.next.next.data is 9.

Conclusion:


The output of Line 1 is 7, and the output of Line 2 is 9.

questions.qtext: Given a circular, doubly-linked list whose contents are sorted in ascending order, what is the run-time complexity for inserting a new element into the list so that it remains correctly sorted? (Including the time required to search for the element’s correct position.)
questions.solution:
Answer: C

Source solution 1 (score: 34)
It’s better to take the worst case possible

Assume we have $1<->3<->4<->6 <-> 8$

new node to be added is say 5

so to maintain the linked list in the sorted order we have to go to the middle node to insert this new node

which takes $O(N/2) = O(N)$ time if we $N$ elements

so option c is correct
Source solution 2 (score: 4)
total time = time to search suitable postion + time to reach to that position + time to insert node
= O(logn) {Binary search} + O(n) + O(1)
= O(n)
Source solution 3 (score: 3)

Assume you had circular linked list had 1,2,4,5. Suppose you want to insert and element 3 for this you should traverse and insert 3 after 2 because we should maintain sorted list even after inserting it takes approximately O(N/2) time which is O(N) and in worst case you should insert new node after last node which takes O(N) time and insertion takes O(1) which add up’s to O(N).

correct ans)C

Source solution 4 (score: 2)

General case, binary search possible on the array which gives random access of an element but in case of linkedlist it don’t.

Even if we apply binary search, after finding mid() we will have to traverse till mid element that’s why in worst case time complexity would be O(n) instead of O(log n)

Reference:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5281053/how-to-apply-binary-search-olog-n-on-a-sorted-linked-list

Source solution 5 (score: 0)

In above circular doubly linked list if we want to insert a new node 6 then we have to maintain whole linked list as we have to arrange in ascending order and find the correct position.

So, in worst case if we want to insert a new node at the end of a linked list then we have to traverse whole linked list and if it has $N$ elements then it will take $O(N)$ time complexity.

$\color{Green} Ans: C$

Source solution 6 (score: 0)
Suppose we have to insert new node at the end of list then tc would be O(1). The head of circular doubly linked list stores a previous pointer to end node so this can be done in constant time. so what is the worst case scenario here? It would be inserting a node in the middle of list, because either you reach to end node from head and then traverse back through previous pointer or go from the head using next pointer to get at the middle node, it would take O(N/2) which accounts O(N).

A. O(1) – only when we are inserting at end, or on the head
B. O(log N) – This case is never possible in a linked list because even applying Binary Search to find correct position and divide the list in half we would have to traverse the list till middle which is O(N/2) = O(N)
C. O(N) – After insertion at end and in the beginning the situation left is insertion in the middle so this is the correct option
D. O(N^2) – traversing a list twice would never be the case for performing insertion operation

class Node:
 def __init__(self, data, next=None):
 self.data = data
 self.next = next
def print_nodes(ptr):
 if ptr:
 print(ptr.data, end=' ')
 while ptr.next:
 ptr = ptr.next
 print(ptr.data, end=' ')

What is the output, if the address of the first node of singly linked list $1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3\rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 5$ is passed in the above python code?
questions.solution:
Answer: A

Source solution 1 (score: 2)

The given code defines a class Node and a function print_nodes that prints the elements of a singly linked list.
Let's analyze the print_nodes function:

  1. If the input pointer ptr is not None, it prints the data of the first node.
  2. It then enters a while loop that continues as long as ptr.next is not None. Inside the loop, ptr is moved to the next node, and the data of each node is printed.
Given Linked List:

1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5

The first print statement prints the data of the first node: 1.

The while loop then iterates over the remaining nodes, printing their data: 2, 3, 4, and 5.

Output:

The output will be: 1 2 3 4 5, which matches the format 12345.

Correct Answer: A. 12345.

The following code is intended to remove a node p from a doubly linked list. Assume that we know that p is in the list, so the list is not empty.

class Node:
 def __init__(self, value, next=None, prev=None):
 self.value = value
 self.next = next
 self.prev = prev
def remove_node(p, front, rear):
 prev = p.prev
 succ = p.next
 if p == front:
 front = front.next
 if front is None:
 rear = None
 else:
 front.prev = None
 else:
 prev.next = succ
 if p == rear:
 rear = rear.next
 rear.next = None
 else:
 succ.prev = prev
 return front, rear

Given three linked lists (a),(b), and (c) as shown below.



Mark the correct option(s).

options.text: Code will not crash on any of the given linked lists

questions.solution:
Answer: B, C

Source solution 1 (score: 6)

In test case B & C:

We are facing (None.prev) or (None.next), which leads to an AttributeError (similar to a segmentation fault in C). Hence, the test case fails.

So, the correct answers are B and C.
